title: Ten-key USB-C QMK macropad Rev A
raw_request: Engineer, document, and validate a reusable natural-language-to-KiCad PCB design system, then use existing repository references to deliver a manufacturing-ready, working 10-key USB keypad/macropad with evidence, automated checks, firmware, fabrication/assembly outputs, BOM, and validation documentation. Do not claim physical operation before prototype bring-up.

requirements.statement: Provide ten independently reportable keys using a diode-protected 2×5 matrix and default USB HID keycodes F13 through F22.
requirements.verification_method: Schematic/netlist-to-QMK contract audit, firmware compile, then P001 all-key and ghosting test.
requirements.source: User request and canonical matrix architecture

requirements.statement: Operate as a USB 2.0 full-speed bus-powered device from a reversible USB-C receptacle in both plug orientations.
requirements.verification_method: ERC/DRC and topology audit now; P001 current-limited plug-orientation enumeration test before hardware claim.

requirements.statement: Include CC Rd termination, resettable input protection, USB ESD protection, series damping, local decoupling, RESET and ISP recovery.
requirements.verification_method: Evidence/schematic review, exact BOM, and connectivity audit.

requirements.statement: Use a two-layer 101×73 mm board with four M2 holes, 19.05 mm key grid, reviewed placement, GND planes, and documented rules.
requirements.verification_method: Native stats, DRC, render/Gerber review, and mechanical contract.

requirements.statement: Reserve the user-facing front for SW1 through SW10; place every other populated electrical component, including all SMT, reset, ISP, and USB-C, on the underside.
requirements.verification_method: Automated footprint-side audit, top/bottom assembly drawings, 3D renders, and CPL side review.

requirements.statement: Release exact schematic/PCB parity with zero KiCad ERC violations, DRC violations, unconnected items, and schematic-parity issues.
requirements.verification_method: Fresh official KiCad 10 release gates with exit-code enforcement.

requirements.statement: Provide an exact-MPN BOM covering all 44 schematic components and a reviewed SMT placement list.
requirements.verification_method: Automated schematic coverage and CPL count checks plus documented orientation policy.

requirements.statement: Provide reproducibly compiled pinned-QMK ATmega32U4 firmware consistent with hardware matrix/ISP/USB pins and documented recovery.
requirements.verification_method: Pinned container build, SHA-256, and 35-check netlist/firmware contract audit.

requirements.statement: Provide Gerber/drill, BOM, CPL, IPC-D-356, IPC-2581, assembly drawings, STEP, notes, archives, and hashes suitable for supplier DFM/RFQ.
requirements.verification_method: Release verifier, archive CRC/member audit, independent Gerber render, and manifest hash verification.

requirements.statement: Before any working/production claim, fabricate P001 and pass current, rail, clock, USB-orientation, enumeration, DFU/ISP, all-key, ghosting, and soak acceptance tests.
requirements.verification_method: Execute docs/bring-up-plan.md and archive signed measurements/logs.

assumptions.statement: Rev A is a standalone bare-board macropad; enclosure and switch plate are outside scope.
Two-layer 1.6 mm FR-4 and short USB full-speed routing are used without a controlled-impedance claim.
CHERRY MX1A-E1NW PCB-mount switches are inserted from the front/user side after all underside SMT assembly; all populated non-switch electronics are on the underside.
Prototype firmware uses VID/PID FEED:0010 only for internal P001 bring-up.

open_questions.question: How is the USB-C VBUS via-in-pad fabrication blocker removed?
open_questions.answer: J1 was changed to GCT USB4085-GF-A. Its contacts are plated through-holes and its VBUS escapes use ordinary external vias, so no VIPPO process remains. J1 requires a separate THT/wave-selective/manual assembly step.

open_questions.question: Which owned USB VID/PID will be used commercially?
open_questions.answer: None is assigned in Rev A. FEED:0010 is explicitly prototype-only; commercial distribution is prohibited until an owned/authorized identity is substituted and firmware is rebuilt.

open_questions.question: Does the board fit an enclosure or plate?
open_questions.answer: Not claimed; Rev A scope is bare-board. A future enclosure release must obtain switch models and complete an independent mechanical fit check.
